name: React

hook.title: Your React code, on Pyreon's engine.
hook.lede: `@pyreon/react-compat` covers React 19's public API with near-full parity, and it runs the value-and-re-render model you know: `useState` returns the value, the body re-runs, deps arrays are honoured. Most components move over with their imports untouched.

covers: React's hook rules: positional hooks, deps arrays, stale-closure semantics.
Pyreon's own components work inside a compat app: the router, query, form, toast, head and UI providers ship marked with `nativeCompat()` (33 components across 17 packages).
doesNotCover: Class components: `Component` and `PureComponent` are stubs; `setState` and `forceUpdate` warn and do nothing, lifecycle methods never fire.

Nested state across a parent re-render: the parent rebuilds its subtree, so a child's `useState`, `useReducer` and `useRef` reset and `useEffect([])` runs again. `memo` does not stop it; lift the state up.

`react-dom` resolves to `@pyreon/react-compat/dom`, which exports `createRoot` and `render` only. Import `createPortal` and `flushSync` from `react`; `hydrateRoot` and `react-dom/server` are not provided.
Libraries that use React internals or its scheduler: `zustand/react`'s `useStore`, `@xyflow/react`, the heavier `react-aria` hooks. Prefer a `/vanilla` or `/core` entry where one exists.
`version` reports `19.0.0-pyreon`, so code that checks for an exact React version will not match.
A few React 19 exports: `useEffectEvent`, `<Activity>`, `<ViewTransition>` and `cache` are not provided, so an import of them fails.

config.note: Use it in place of `@vitejs/plugin-react`. Aliases `react`, `react/jsx-runtime`, `react-dom` and `react-dom/client`.
Types and the JSX runtime come from the compat package.

ports.title: Then, one component at a time

after.label: Pyreon

ports.note: The Pyreon side is the final form, after `compat` is switched off. While the app is still in compat mode, wrap it in `nativeCompat()` and write the text as an arrow (`{() => …}`), as in step 4 on /migrate.
